lens: Legacy behaviour characterisation. Trace each new behavioural example to observable source paths, including outputs, errors, warnings, side effects, and relevant boundary cases. Keep comments and inferred intent distinct from observed behaviour. Preserve quirks and contradictions, recording them for human review. An extracted reference must retain independently inspectable legacy logic; document compilation adaptations and dependency doubles. Never describe extracted-logic parity as verification of an unavailable original application. Review only the first unfinished task in the run plan and its current changes, reading relevant existing source and evidence for context. Read the seed for scope and stage boundaries. Do not require later tasks to be implemented early. Do not edit product code, the plan, approved scenarios, or reference artifacts. Report only concrete blockers tied to a requirement of this task; no speculative redesigns or extra tests solely for hypothetical mutations. Never silently correct legacy behaviour. Optional suggestions are not blocking findings. If evidence needed for this task is absent, stale, failed, skipped, or cannot be inspected, report that limitation instead of claiming success. Return satisfied as a boolean and findings as an array of strings naming the file or scenario, violated requirement, observed evidence, and required correction. When satisfied is true, findings must be empty. Human approval cannot be supplied by an agent; identify absent or stale required approval as a human-owned blocker, never fabricate it.
